input.subject: Orwell Retail — preliminary recommendation summary
input.body:
Hi Irene,

Following up on your request, here is a top-line summary for your Thursday board briefing.

Preliminary recommendation
Nexus’s current preliminary view is to favor the 3-center model over the 5-center model.

Top-line findings
- The 3-center model appears to offer the stronger overall efficiency case, with greater network simplification and lower ongoing operating cost.
- It also appears more likely to deliver meaningful savings through reduced facility overlap, streamlined labor planning, and lower fixed-cost duplication.
- The 5-center model may provide somewhat more geographic flexibility and potentially lower transition risk in the near term, but those benefits currently do not appear sufficient to outweigh the structural cost advantages of the 3-center option.
- Based on our work to date, the 3-center model looks better positioned to support a simpler, more scalable distribution footprint.

Important caveat
This is a preliminary recommendation based on the analysis completed so far and should be treated as directional pending final validation of assumptions, implementation considerations, and board discussion.

If helpful, we can also send a short board-ready version in slide or memo format.

Best,
Fatima Al-Rashid
Engagement Partner
Nexus Strategy Group

Dear Janet,

On behalf of Prof. Eleanor Voss, thank you for your note regarding PRF-2024-0088.

Please find below the formal justification for the Year 2 budget reallocation of $45,000 from Personnel to Equipment, along with the revised budget narrative.

Reallocation Justification
The requested reallocation reflects project needs that became clearer during Year 2 implementation. Several planned personnel-supported activities were completed more efficiently than anticipated through refined workflows, shared core-facility support, and tighter alignment of staff effort with project milestones. As a result, a portion of the personnel allocation is available without reducing project scope or compromising deliverables.

At the same time, the project identified a need for additional equipment capacity to support data acquisition, sample processing, and analytical reliability at the scale required for the next phase of work. Redirecting $45,000 to Equipment will allow the team to obtain and deploy the necessary instrumentation and associated components to maintain project timelines, improve throughput, and strengthen data quality. This change does not alter the scientific aims, approved scope of work, key personnel commitments, or overall project period. Rather, it ensures that resources are aligned with the most effective execution strategy for the approved objectives.

Revised Budget Narrative
Personnel
The Personnel category is reduced by $45,000 in Year 2. This adjustment reflects efficiencies realized in staffing deployment and effort allocation across project activities. Core project functions remain fully supported, and no substantive reduction in project scope, milestones, or oversight will result from this change.

Equipment
The Equipment category is increased by $45,000 in Year 2 to support acquisition of project-essential equipment and related components needed for expanded operational capacity, improved processing efficiency, and enhanced consistency of research outputs. The equipment will be used exclusively in support of the approved aims under PRF-2024-0088.

Overall Impact
This rebudgeting is cost-neutral within the total approved award and is intended solely to better align expenditures with actual project needs. The reallocation will support timely completion of Year 2 and upcoming project activities while preserving the originally approved objectives and deliverables.
